l. In exercise of powers conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section (l) and Sub-section (2A) of Section 0 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (/4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour and 
Employment, vide its Order No. L-420/225/208-IR (DU) dated 3.02.20l9 has been pleased to refer the 
following dispute between the employer, that is the Management of North Delhi Municipal Corporation and their 
workman for adjudication by this Tribunal, terms of which are as under: 


“Whether non-payment of wages by the management of North Delhi Municipal Corporation to Sh. Vikram 
Singh Rana S/o Sh. Harpal Singh Rana, Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 07.07.7994 in the pay scale of Rs. 950- 
4500/- revised from time to time attached to the said post with all consequential benefits upto 37.॥2.207, 
the date of superannuation as per direction of he Hon’ble High Court vide order dated 27.06, 2073 is illegal 
and unjustified? If so, what directions are necessary in this respect?” 


In pursuance to the reference, claimant had filed the claim statement stated that he has been employed on Muster 
Roll Mali on 2.05.982. Thereafter, he was initially appointed as regular Mali on 03.0i.985. He had been 
performing the duty of an Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0.994 till his superannuation up to 3l.2.20I7 under Rohini 
Zone (Horticulture) under North Delhi Municipal Corporation. Management has fixed the different pay scales to 
their employees including Mali, Chaudhary etc. in accordance to their job profile. He was not given the grant of 
proper pay scale of officiating Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0i.994 to 3.2.20l7 which amount to force labour and the 
management is indulging in unfair labour practice. He had got the payment in lower pay scale of Mali Rs. 750-940/- 
revised from time to time and he has been denied the pay scale of Rs. 950-500/- for his duty performed as 
Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0.994 revised from time to time. He had stated that Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in the matter 
of Jai Chand vs. MCD (CW No. 654/200) has disapproved the non-payment vide order dated 02.05.2003 for the 
post of Chaudhary. The same stand has been taken by the Hon’ble Division Bench of High Court of Delhi in the 
matter of MCD vs. Sultan Singh & Ors. in W.P. (C) No. 7947/200. As such, he claims that he may be awarded 
the payment of Acting Chaudhary in the pay scale of Rs. 950-l500/- revised from time to time to him w.e.f. 
0I.0.994 up to his superannuation. 


2. Respondent herein has filed the ४४.७. stating that the claimant does not disclose the correct facts and has filed the 
claim without any locus. Workman is not eligible for any kind of relief as prayed by him in the present application 
and the said application is nothing but an abuse of process of law and waste of precious judicial time. It has been 
submitted by him that workman was promoted as a Chaudhary in September, 204 and on his retirement he had 
already received all the consequential benefit of his retirement. He submitted that there is no such provision in the 
tules of the respondent management of giving benefits of acting Chaudhary to the claimant because it is merely a 
change of work and administrative arrangement and not a promotion. He further submitted that workman is trying to 
misguide the court by showing the internal office record of the management whereas he has no such authority to use 
the official documents of the management, the same being for internal use of the management. He had denied that 
the management has fixed any pay scale for officiating Chaudhary. However, he had admitted that there are different 
pay scales for different posts. He further denied that Mali and Chawkidar who are performing their duty as Acting 
Chaudhary were granted the pay scale of Chaudhary. He submitted that claim petition be dismissed. 


3. After completion of pleadings vide order dated 4.08.209, following issues had been framed: 


a. Whether the NDMC illegally refused to grant the revised pay scale to the workman w.e.f. 0.0.94 in the post of 
acting Choudhary. 


b. Whether the management illegally denied such revised pay scale to the workman upto 3!.2.20I7 the date of his 
superannuation ignoring the direction of the Hon’ble High Court vide order dated 27.08.203. 


c. To what relief the claimant is entitled to. 


4. In order to prove its claim, the workman himself had entered into the witness box. He deposed the fact that he was 
allotted the work of an Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 0.0.994 and performed his duty under Rohini Zone 
(Horticulture) till his superannuation up to 3!..20l7. His name has been appearing at Serial No. 25 in the list of 
officiating Chaudhary issued by the Dy. Director (Horticulture) West Zone which is Exhibit १४७१/॥. He submitted 
that he is entitled to the wages of Acting Chaudhary in the pay scale of Rs. 950-500 revised from time to time w.e-f. 
0I.0.994 up to 3.2.207 along with all consequential benefits. 


5. Witness was put to the cross-examination where he admitted that he had never lodged any complaint in the office 
of the management claiming his unpaid dues which is the subject matter of the present proceeding since he was told 


5892 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


that his matter shall be taken up by the management with the case of similarly placed person. In the year 204 he has 
got the promotion to the post of supervisor from the post of Mali. He had filed the document which has been marked 
as Ex. १४५७४|/।. This document was given to him by the management and he did not have the original. He had denied 
that the claim has been filed on the basis of false and fabricated document. 


6. In rebuttal, one Sh. Rakesh Kumar, Assitant Director (Horticulture), Rohini Zone, MCD has been examined by 
the counsel of the management, wherein he had reiterated the facts and mentioned by him in the W.S. He had 
admitted that initially he had joined the MCD at the post of Maali. Thereafter, he was promoted to the post of 
Assistant Director in January, 2024. He admitted that Ex. ४ै/७४॥/|, the list of workmen including the workman in 
question who had been shown at Serial No. 25 as Acting Chaudhary. He stated that the list pertain to the west zone. 
West Zone was bifurcated and one of the zone was known as Rohini Zone. 


7. Ihave heard the argument at par, perused the record and analyzed the evidence. The whole of the case of the 
claimant rest upon the fact that management witness has admitted the list Ex. ४४/५७॥/| wherein name of the workman 
had been shown at S.No. 25. He was 0" pass, appointed as “Mali” on 03.0.985 and looking after the work of 
Acting Chaudhary w.e.f. 0!.0!.994. He had made prayer that considering the above facts on record and in view of 
the judgment passed by the Hon’ble High Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs. Sultan Singh & 
others W.P. (C) No. 7947 of 200, decided on 20.04.20ll where similarly placed person had been given the higher 
scale so he be given the pay scale of Acting Chaudhary revised from time to time. 


8. While the respondent stand is that the workman’s service was earlier regularized as Mali in [985 and he was 
promoted in the year September, 204 and till then he has been paid all the benefit of the Acting Chaudhary. He was 
retired in the year 207 and he had been paid all the benefits therein. He further submits that workman is not entitled 
to the benefit for the pay scale of the Acting Chaudhary. 


9. Here, it is not disputed that the claimant has not been working as Acting Chaudhary since 994. MW himself 
admitted the list issued by management where the name of the claimant has been shown as I0" pass and has been 
working as an Acting Chaudhary since 994. Operating portion of the judgment of Sultan Singh & Others in which 
the workman has placed reliance, where in para no. 28, it was observed: 


“28. Considering the entire facts and circumstances it is apparent that the claim of the respondents have 
always been that they should be paid the difference in pay of Mali/Chowkidar and the Garden Chaudhary 
as they were made to work on the post of Garden Chaudhary whereas the petitioner had first denied that 
they worked as Garden Chaudharies, then took the plea that the Assistant Director (Horticulture) was not 
competent to ask the respondents to work as Garden Chaudharies and that the respondents cannot be 
appointed to the post of Garden Chaudharies in accordance with the recruitment rules. There is no doubt 
that respondents are not claiming appointment to the post of Garden Chaudharies on account of having 
worked on ad-hoc basis on the post of Garden Chaudhary contrary to rules or that some of them not 
having the requisite qualifications are entitled for relaxation.” 


0. It is not out of place mention here that even if the claimant herein was not a party in Sultan’s case referred 
above, judgment of Hon’ble High Court is binding on the management and the management is required to implement 
the same. When the workman had been assigned the job of an ‘Acting Chaudhary’ i.e. a higher post then that of 
‘Mali’ for so long (for the last 20 years), he should have been designated as Acting Chaudhary. However, if that was 
not done, then he would also be entitled for the pay scale of an Acting Chaudhary instead of Mali. 


ll. In the light of above discussion, issue no. | decided against the management and in favour of the workman. 
Issue no. 2 is also decided against the management and in favour of the workman. 


2. In view of the above, workman/claimant is entitled to the pay scale of Acting Chaudhary since 994 to 204, 
when he was actually promoted to the post. Respondent herein is liable to pay the difference of the wages of Mali 
and Acting Chaudhary from the date, when the workman herein was performing duty till he was actually promoted, 
management is directed to pay the entire difference of the salary within two months from the date of passing the 
award. Award is passed accordingly. A copy of this award is sent to the appropriate government for notification as 
required under section I7 of the I.D Act, 947.

AWARD 


In exercise of power conferred under clause (d) of Sub-section () and Sub-section (2A) of Section l0 of 
the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (4 of 947), the Government of India through the Ministry of Labour, vide its 
Order No. L-2202/38/2000-IR(C-ID dated 02.08.200I has been pleased to refer the following dispute between 
the employer, that is the Management of Madhabpur Colliery under Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited and 
their workman for adjudication by this Tribunal. 


“ Whether the action of the management of Madhavpur Colliery of M/s. ECL in dismissing Sh. Rajkumar 
Singh, Pit Clerk from services w.e.f. /3.3.93 is legal and justified? If not, to what relief the workman is 
entitled to ? ” 


l. On receiving Order No. L-2202/38/2000-IR(C-ID) dated 02.08.200l from the Government of India, 
Ministry of Labour, New Delhi for adjudication of the dispute, a Reference case was registered on 0.09.200I/ 
9..200] and an order was passed for issuing notice to the parties through registered post, directing them to 
appear and submit their written statements along with relevant documents in support of their claims. 


2; Mr. Rakesh Kumar, the then General Secretary of Koyala Mazdoor Congress filed written statement on 
20.02.2002 on behalf of Rajkumar Singh, the dismissed workman of Madhabpur Colliery under Kajora Area of 
Eastern Coalfields Limited (hereinafter referred to as ECL). In brief, the fact of the case disclosed in the written 
statement of the union is that Rajkumar Singh was a permanent employee of ECL and was working as an 
Attendance Clerk at Madhabpur Colliery. On 5.05.!993 he was dismissed from his service without observing 
necessary formalities as per standing orders of the company and without holding any enquiry. Further case of the 
union is that on 4.05.993 an incident took place in connection with which he was charged by the management 


594 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA AUGUST 6, 2025/SHRAVANA 25, 947 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


but no Charge Sheet was issued and without holding any domestic enquiry the workman was dismissed form his 
service on the basis of a prima facie enquiry. No second Show Cause Notice was issued to the workman which is a 
mandatory requirement as per a decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India. It is contended that Rajkumar 
Singh has no involvement in the case for which he was dismissed and urged that the order of dismissal issued 
against him is illegal and the same is liable to be set aside. Union has prayed for re-instatement of the workman 
with full back wages. 


3; Management initially did not file any written statement and the case was fixed up for ex-parte hearing. 
Thereafter management filed written statement on 25.03.2003. According to the management of ECL, Rajkumar 
Singh while on duty had taken a Dumper bearing No. WB39-I50] loaded with eight tons of coal from Madhabpur 
Colliery and he himself drove the Dumper towards the railway crossing of Kajoragram where he was caught by the 
security guard of railway site. For the aforesaid act of misconduct Rajkumar Singh was chargesheeted by the 
management under Clause |7(i)(a), !7(i)G) and 7(i)(q) of the Model Standing Orders applicable to the Mine. The 
workman submitted reply to the Charge Sheet but as the reply was not satisfactory a domestic enquiry was ordered 
against him and the Enquiry Officer held the enquiry in which the workman participated. Reasonable opportunity 
was given to the workman to defend himself. The Enquiry Officer observed the principles of natural justice and 
after concluding the enquiry proceeding submitted his report before the Appointing Authority. The charge of 
misconduct was duly proved against Rajkumar Singh. After careful consideration of the Charge Sheet, Enquiry 
Proceeding, Enquiry Report and other connected papers, the Disciplinary Authority dismissed the workman 
from service. Management contended that the contents of paragraph no. 3 of the written statement filed by the 
union is incorrect and that the workman was not dismissed without holding any enquiry. Management denied that 
the workman was dismissed from service without service of Charge Sheet and without holding any domestic 
enquiry. According to the management dismissal of the workman is totally justified and the workman is not 
entitled to any relief. 


4. Rajkumar Singh has been examined as Workman Witness No. |. He has filed affidavit-in-chief wherein 
he stated that on 4.05.993 he was on duty in the second shift from 04.00 PM to 2.00 AM at Madhabpur 
Colliery. After completing his duty, he was proceeding towards his quarters at Khas Kajora Colliery, Madhabpur 
Railway siding on the way to his quarter at Khas Kajora Colliery. At about !2 at night when he reached the 
Railway Crossing at Kajoragram he saw a Dumper was intercepted. He was held up at that place without knowing 
the fact and was handed over to the police and subsequently forwarded to the Jail. It is contended that the 
management did not take any action against the driver who was on duty and drove the Dumper, leaving it at the 
Railway Crossing. Further case of the workman is that the management decided to dismiss him on the same date 
ie., on 5.05.993 without holding any enquiry and without giving him any opportunity to defend his case before 
the Enquiry Officer. The dismissed workman contended that management dismissed him from service on the basis 
of prejudice and no second Show Cause Notice was issued to him as per guidelines issued by the Coal India 
Limited. The workman averred that the order of dismissal passed against him is illegal and unjustified. 


5. Management cross-examined the witness where he deposed that Police lodged an FIR against him and 
submitted Charge Sheet after investigation and the case is pending before the Court at Durgapur. Witness further 
deposed that since he was in custody he never appeared in any Domestic Enquiry. It transpires from the evidence 
that he received Charge Sheet from the management through the Jail Authority and after his release from jail he 
submitted an application before the management regarding non-supply of Charge Sheet and other documents. 
Witness denied that he has been rightly dismissed by the management and volunteered that he was dismissed while 
he was in custody. 

6. From the record as well as order dated 02.07.20l3 it appears that management did not adduce any 
evidence in this case after several opportunity granted to them. On the date of hearing of argument, the order of 
dismissal dated 5.05.!993 has been admitted by both parties and marked as Exhibit ४-।. 


7. The moot question in this case is whether the dismissal of workman from service under ECL is 
sustainable under the law. If not, what relief the workman is entitled to? 

8. Mr. Rakesh Kumar, Union representative argued that the workman has been dismissed form service 
without holding any enquiry. The allegation against him was theft of 8 tonnes of coal, taken away by the workman 
with the help of a Dumper on 4.05.993. The workman was arrested and was kept in jail custody for about a 
month till he was released on bail. The management without issuing any Charge Sheet and without holding any 
enquiry against him dismissed him from service on the very next date vide order dated 5.05.993 (Exhibit W-). 
The union representative urged that such act of dismissal of workman is arbitrary, violative of the principles of 
natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside. 

9. Mr. P. K. Das, learned advocate for the management of ECL admitted that the management is unable to 
produce any Charge Sheet or Enquiry Proceeding on the basis on which the order of dismissal was passed by the 
General Manager. It is submitted that the workman committed theft in respect of the employer’s property and he 
was found guilty of the charge under Clause !7(i)(a) of Model Standing Orders. It is argued that the workman is 
not entitled to any relief in this case as he has committed a criminal offence. 


[भाग Il—ave 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : अगस्त 6, 2025/श्रावण 25, 947 595 


0. I have considered the facts and circumstances of the case and arguments advanced by the union 
representative and learned advocate of the management. It is undisputed that Rajkumar Singh was working as 
Attendance Clerk at Madhabpur Colliery and he was dismissed from his service by order dated 5.05.993, issued 
by the General Manager, Kajora Area bearing No. KA:PM:C-6:0/387/288, in which he has stated that Rajkumar 
Singh had allegedly taken Dumper No. WB39-50] loaded with 8 tonnes of coal from Pit No. 2 of Madhabpur 
Colliery and drove towards the Railway Crossing of Kajoragram and that he was caught with the Dumper by 
Security Guard Mr. Rajdeo Ahir and Md. Daud Khan of Madhabpur Colliery who were on duty at Madhabpur 
Colliery Siding. On receipt to the report, the Agent, Madhabpur Colliery appointed an Enquiry Officer to conduct 
the enquiry into the alleged misconduct. It is further stated in the order of dismissal that the enquiry was conducted 
in presence of Rajkumar Singh and statements were recorded. The Enquiry Officer thereafter submitted his report 
and after going through the Enquiry Report it was found that Rajkumar Singh committed the misconduct under 
Clause 7(i)(a), [7@)(@) and 7(i)(q) of the Model Standing Orders applicable to the company. It is further stated 
that after careful consideration of the report of the Enquiry Officer, connected papers and gravity of misconduct, 
the General Manager dismissed the workman. No Charge Sheet, Enquiry Proceeding has been produced by the 
management to establish that a proper enquiry proceeding was held before the workman was found guilty of the 
charge. There is no iota of evidence to indicate that the workman had opportunity to represent his case. Under such 
facts and circumstances, I hold that the dismissal of Rajkumar Singh on the strength of letter KA:PM:C- 
6:0/387/288 dated 5.05.993, issued by the General Manager, Kajora Area is arbitrary and found unsustainable 
under the law and in violation of principles of natural justice. The workman having been dismissed in an illegal 
manner is entitled to be reinstated. It is appropriate to set aside the order of dismissal dated 5.05.993. The 
workman is entitled to be reinstated in service within two (2) months from the date of communication of the 
Award, if has not attained the age of superannuation till date. It transpires from the materials in record and 
admission of the workman that he was in jail custody and a criminal case is pending against him. The workman has 
not rendered service to the employer company since !5.05.993. Therefore, I am not inclined to grant him full 
back wages for the period he remained idle. It is found appropriate to grant him twenty percent (20%) of his back 
wages from [5.05.993 till his reinstatement in service or superannuation, whichever is earlier. 


Hence, 
ORDERED 


that the Industrial Dispute is allowed on contest against the management of Madhabpur Colliery under 
Kajora Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited. The order of dismissal of Rajkumar Singh, Pit Clerk of Madhabpur 
Colliery is set aside. Management of ECL is directed to reinstate the workman within two (2) months from the date 
of communication of the Award, if the workman has not attained the age of superannuation in the meantime. The 
management shall also pay back wages to the workman at the rate of twenty percent (20%) from 5.05.993 till his 
reinstatement or superannuation whichever is earlier. Let an award be drawn up in light of my above findings. Let 
copies of the Award in duplicate be sent to the Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India, New Delhi for information and 
Notification. 


ANANDA KUMAR MUKHERJEE, Presiding Officer

Subedar Major (Pharmacist), Subedar (Pharmacist), except as respects to things done or omitted to be done before 
such supersession, the Central Government hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to 
the posts of Subedar Major (Pharmacist), Subedar (Pharmacist) and Naib Subedar (Pharmacist), in the Assam Rifles 
in the Ministry of Home Affairs, namely:- 


0 Short title and commencement.— (l) These rules may be called the Ministry of Home Affairs, Assam 
Rifles, Subedar Major (Pharmacist), Subedar (Pharmacist) and Naib Subedar (Pharmacist), Group ‘B’ Posts, 
Recruitment Rules 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application.— These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column () of the Scheduled annexed to 
these rules. 


3. Number of posts, classification and level in the pay matrix.— The number of the said posts, their 
classification and level in pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule. 


4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.__ The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (3) of the said 
Schedule. 


5. Disqualification.— No person, — 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 


(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, shall be eligible 
for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


6. Superannuation.— () Every person appointed under these rules shall retire from service on the afternoon of 
the last day of the month in which he or she attains the age of sixty years or as prescribed by the Central Government 
from time to time: 


Provided that a person whose date of birth is on the first day of the month, shall retire from service in the 
afternoon of the last day of the preceding month on attaining the age of superannuation. 


(2) No person shall be granted extension in service beyond the prescribed age of retirement on 
superannuation as specified in sub-rule (). 


7. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, 
it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


8. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, Ex-servicemen 
and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to 
time in this regard.

New Delhi, the 5th August, 2025 


G.S.R. 29.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Shrimati Sucheta Kriplani Hospital, New Delhi Pharmacist 
(Group ‘C’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 20I9, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such 
supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of 
Pharmacist in the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Shrimati Sucheta Kriplani Hospital, New Delhi, under the 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, namely:- 


I. Short title and commencement.— (|) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Lady Hardinge Medical College and Shrimati Sucheta Kriplani Hospital, New Delhi, Pharmacist (Group ‘C’ Post) 
Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix.— The number of the said post, its classification 
and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to 


these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.__ The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (3) of the said 
Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.— No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 


any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, 
it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to 


any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, ex-Servicemen 
and other special categories of persons, in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to 


time in this regard.

G.S.R. 30.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, Senior Technical Officer and Senior Perfusionist, 
Group ‘B’ Post, Recruitment Rules, 2007, in so far as it relates to the post of ‘Senior Perfusionist’, except as respects 
things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating 
the method of recruitment to the post of Senior Perfusionist in the Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, 
under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, namely:- 


l. Short title and commencement.— (l) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, Senior Perfusionist (Group ‘B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 
2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix.— The number of the said posts, their classification 
and level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (I3) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.— No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required 
to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the ex-Servicemen and 
other special categories of persons, in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time 


in this regard.

Technologist in the Radiotherapy Department of the Lady Hardinge Medical College and Shrimati Sucheta Kriplani 
Hospital, New Delhi, under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, namely: - 


l. Short title and commencement.— (|) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Lady 
Hardinge Medical College and Shrimati Sucheta Kriplani Hospital, New Delhi, Senior Radiotherapy Technologist 
(Group ‘B’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2025.

in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (/3) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.— No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
such person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, 
relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Ex-Servicemen and other 
special categories of person in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

G.S.R. 33.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, the 
President hereby makes the following rules, regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Deputy Chief 
Physiotherapist in the Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, namely:- 


. Short title and commencement.— (l) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi, Deputy Chief Physiotherapist (Group ‘A’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix.— The number of the said post, its classification and level 
in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (/3) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification.— No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 


(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax.— Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, 
relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving.— Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to be 
provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen and other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in 
this regard.

special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in 
this regard.

G.S.R. 36.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the constitution, the 
President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Library and 
Information Officer in the NITI Aayog, namely:- 


l. Short title and commencement. — (|) These rules may be called the NITI Aayog, (Library and Information 
Officer) Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in the pay matrix.- The number of the post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to 
these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age- limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating thereto shall be as specified in column (5) to (43) of the said 
Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person; 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, 
it may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, ex- 
servicemen and other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central 
Government from time to time in this regard.

3. The brief facts of the case of the applicant is that he was permanent employee of M/s. BCCL and was

charge sheet, the applicant submitted his reply and denied the allegations levelled against him, although the 
explanation submitted by him was satisfactory but even then the management initiated departmental proceeding 
against him by appointing Enquiry Officer. Thereafter the Enquiry Officer conducted domestic enquiry in utter 
violation of the principle of natural justice and submitted a perverse report and relying on the same, the 
disciplinary authority issued him a second show cause notice on 08.05.20l9. The applicant submitted his 
explanation to the second show cause notice on 4.05.209 but without considering the same, the disciplinary 
authority imposed the penalty of dismissal which is shockingly disproportionate and illegal vide order dated 
0.06.209. After the dismissal, the applicant preferred an appeal on .07.209 under order 30 of the Certified

of the workman from his serviceis shockingly disproportionate and therefore, considering that the workman is very

On the other hand the Ld. Counsel of the management has submitted that the applicant is a habitual

8. After hearing the rival submissions of both the parties and perusing the materials on record the Tribunal 
finds that the following two issues are necessary to be decided:- 


(i) Whether the domestic enquiry was fair and proper? 


(ii) Whether the action of the management of Dhansar/Industry Colliery under Kusunda Area of M/s BCCL 
in dismissing Sri Binod Kumar Manjhi, Ex-General Mazdoor vide dismissal letter dated 0-06-209, is legal and 
justified? And if not to what relief the workman concerned Sri Binod Kumar Manjhi is entitled? 


As regards the first issue, the applicant/workman by filing application dated 24.03.202, has accepted and 
admitted the enquiry report against him as fair and proper u/s IlA of the I.D. Act, 947 and accordingly the 
Tribunal vide order dated 6.2.202] also held that the enquiry against the applicant was fair and proper and thus

by admitting the enquiry report as fair and proper the workman has accepted that he remained absent from 
2.2.208 to 9.02.20I9 from his duty without giving any prior information or taking permission of the 
management which comes under the category of misconduct vide Certified Standing Order No. 26..l of the 
BCCL (Exhibit M-5). 


Now, the second issue for consideration is whether the punishment imposed on the workman is legal and 
justified or disproportionate, in this regard the documentary evidence of the workman which has been marked as 
Exhibit W-|, shows that this is dismissal order dated 0.06.209 from the service of the applicant/workman, Binod 
Kumar Manjhi, General Mazdoor, Dhansar Colliery and on its perusal it is evident that the workman has been 
dismissed from his service on the ground of being habitual absentee and in the same order it has been described 
that on four earlier occasions also, the workman remained absent from his duty without any prior information and 
permission by the management and these are from 6.08.206 to 24.l0.206 for which he has been given strong 
warning for absence from his duty for about two months, from |.07.20l7 to 04.!.20l7 for which his one salary 
increment was stopped due to absence from his duty for about four months, from 9.02.20l8 to 04.07.208 for 
which he was given punishment of stoppage of one salary increment for being absent for about five months, from 
02..20I8 to 03.2.20l8 he was given punishment of strong warning for absence from his duty for about one 
month and again in the instant case he remained absent from 2.2.20I8 to 9.02.20l9 without any information 
and permission of the management and remained absent for about two months and seven days and in view of the 
repeated and habitual absence of the applicant from his duty, ultimately he was dismissed by the management. 


As regards other documentary evidence of the workman, Exhibit W-2 is anapplication for joining dated 
20.02.209, Exhibit W-4is the second show cause notice dated 08.05.209, Exhibit W-5 is the mercy appeal dated 
03.07.209 before General Manager, Kusunda Area of M/s. BCCL, Exhibit W-6 is an application for raising the 
Industrial Dispute before Assistant Labour Commissioner, Dhanbad and Exhibit W-7 is the photo copy of the first 
page ofpass book of the Bank Account of the workman but all these documents are not going to help the applicant 
in any way. 


Now as regards the Medical Certificate which is Exhibit W-3, on its perusal it transpires that Dr. M. Prasad has 
certified on 9.02.20l9 that the workman Binod Kumar Manjhi was suffering from Jaundice and weakness from 
2.2.208 to 9.02.20l9 whereas the applicant/workman has himself stated in his rejoinder petition that he 
remained absent from his duty due to the illness of his wife and at the same time Exhibit M-6 and M-I] which is 
reply of the charge sheet and reply of 2"! show cause notice of the applicant Binod Kumar Manjhi, he has himself 
written in his own writing that his wife fell ill in his village and due to the same he could not perform his duty thus, 
these documents reveal that the ground of defence of the workman regarding his absence is self contradictory. 


As regards the documentary evidences of the management, Exhibit M-l to M-4 are the office order dated 
3/4..206, 05.2.207, 22/23.08.208 and 06.2.208 by which the workman Binod Kumar Manjhi has been 
earlier punished due to his absence from his duty without information and prior permission, so these documents 
reveal that the workman has been habitual absentee from his duty. Exhibit M-5 is the charge sheet dated 
03.0I.209 issued by the management against the applicant Binod Kumar Manjhi. Exhibit M-6 is the reply of 
charge sheet dated 03.0!.209 and Exhibit M-I is the reply of second show cause notice and in both these hand 
written documents the applicant has taken the defence that his wife was ill. Exhibit M-7 is notice of enquiry, 
Exhibit M-8 is enquiry proceeding, Exhibit M-9 is enquiry report. Exhibit M-l3 is the dismissal order of the 
applicant which has also been submitted by the applicant and marked as Exhibit ४-] in his favour. Exhibit १-0 is 
a second show cause notice and Exhibit M-2 is a note sheet. 


9. The Ld. Counsel for the applicant has relied on and cited the authority of the Hon’ble Karnataka High 
Court reported in 208 LLR 507 (Mr. A Lokesh Vs. M/s. Otto Bliz (India) Pvt. Ltd.) in which the Hon’ble 
Court has been pleased to hold that “Punishmentof dismissal from service on account of sickness supported by 
medical certificate is not justified.” but here in the instant case the facts and circumstances are completely different 
and it has already been proved by the rejoinder petition of the applicant as well as Exhibit M-6 and M-I] of the OP 
that thedefence of sickness of the applicant on the ground of his Medical Certificate, is quite contradictory and 
discrepant as he has claimed in Exhibit M-6 and M-! that he remained absent due to illness of his wife and on the 
other hand he has submitted the Medical Certificate of his own sickness and therefore, this Tribunal is of the 
opinion that the above authority of the Hon’ble Karnataka High Court is not applicable in the present facts and 
circumstances of the case of the applicant. 


On the other hand,on perusal of the authority of the Hon’ble Apex Court incase of Maan Singh vs Union 
of India, reported in AIR 2003 supreme court 800,it is evident that habitual absenteeism without leave is 
sufficient to provide major punishment of dismissal. 


In another case namely Om Prakash Vs State of Punjab &Ors reported in(20l) 4 SCC 682, the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court has held that habitual absentee without leave does not deserve any sympathy from the 
court.

0. Considering the above facts, circumstancesand evidence available on the case record (Ext. W-l,Ext. W-3,

quoted authorities of the Hon’ble supreme court, this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the action of dismissal 
of the workman Binod Kumar Manjhi by the management of Dhansar Colliery under Kusunda Area of M/s. BCCL 
vide dismissal order dated 0.06.209, is legal and justifiedand is quite proportionate to the repeated incorrigible 
misconduct committed by the workman and there is no mitigating circumstance in favour of the workman to avoid 
the punishment of dismissal from service and therefore, this application of the applicant/workman is liable to be 
dismissed.

G.S.R. 137.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Government Medical Store Depot (Group ‘C’ and Group 'D' posts) Recruitment Rules, 1983, in so 
far as it relates to the post of Pharmacist-cum-Clerk, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such 
supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of 
Pharmacist-cum-Clerk in the Government Medical Store Depot located at New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, 
Hyderabad, Guwahati and Karnal namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. -(1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Government Medical Store Depots, Pharmacist-cum-Clerk (Group ‘C’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. —The number of the said post, its classification and level 
in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc. - The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. — No person, — 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post; 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


5. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class 
or category of persons. 


6. Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex-servicemen or other 
special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in 
this regard.

New Delhi, the 14th August, 2025 


G.S.R. 138.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, and in the 
supersession of the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Professor (Sugar Engineering), Assistant Professor (Sugar 
Engineering), Lecturer (Sugar Engineering), Assistant Engineer (Electrical / Mechanical Engineering) and Senior 
Research Assistant (Mechanical Engineering) Recruitment Rules, 2017, in so far they relate to the posts of Assistant 
Engineer (Electrical) and Assistant Engineer (Mechanical), except as respects things done or omitted to be done 
before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the 
posts of Assistant Engineer (Electrical) and Assistant Engineer (Mechanical) in National Sugar Institute, Kanpur 
under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distributions, Department of Food and Public Distribution, 
namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the National Sugar Institute, Kanpur, Assistant 
Engineer (Electrical) and Assistant Engineer (Mechanical) Recruitment Rules, 2025.

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 

2. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix. — The number of said posts, their classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto, shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to 
these rules. 

3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc The method of recruitment to the said post, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating thereto shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the aforesaid Schedule. 
4. Disqualification. — No person,- 

(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 

(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post. 

Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, 
exempt such person from the operation of this rule. 

5. Power to relax. -Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, and in consultation with UPSC relax any of the provisions of these 
rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 

6. Savings. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Ex-servicemen and other 
categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

such person from the operation of this rule.

by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class 
or category of persons.

be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Ex-servicemen and other 
categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time in this 
regard.

G.S.R. 140.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, and in 
supersession of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Department of Food and Public 
Distribution, National Sugar Institute, Multi-Tasking Staff, Group ‘C’ Posts, Recruitment Rules, 2016, except as 
respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules 
to regulate the method of recruitment to the post of Multi-Tasking Staff, in the National Sugar Institute under 
the Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, 
namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. — (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and 
Public Distribution, Department of Food and Public Distribution, National Sugar Institute, Multi-Tasking Staff, 
(Group ‘C’ Post) Recruitment Rules, 2025. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Number of post, classification and level in pay matrix. —The number of the said post, its classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the Schedule annexed to these 
tules. 


3. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, ete—The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications 
and other matters relating to the said post shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the said Schedule. 


4. Disqualification. -- No person, — 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


me Power to relax. —Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any 
class or category of persons. 


6. Saving. — Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions 
required to be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, other backward classes, ex-servicemen, and 
other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time 
in this regard.

The Central Government, Ministry of Labour & Employment vide its Order No. L-14011/15/2018-IR(DU) 
dated 27.11.2018 referred the following Industrial Dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication. 


Con..2 
The schedule mentioned in that order is: 


“Whether the action of the management of Indian Coast Guard, Base Maintenance Unit, Chennai, in 
transferring Sh. P. Ayan Arul Raj, Radio/Radar Fitter to [CGS Mandapam in an non-existing post at ICGS 
Mandapam is legal and justified? If not, to what relief Sh. P.Ayan Arul Raj, Radio/Radar Fitter is entitled 
to?” 


As per the claim statement the petitioner is an Indian Coast Guard Civilian Employees Union, registered under the 
Trade Union Act, 1926 was formed primarily to protect the interest of the workmen and for the welfare of the 
employees apart from maintaining harmonious relationship with the Management. It is submitted that there are 60 
civilian workmen in the establishment and most of them are members of the Union, this being the only union

functioning in the establishment to espouse the cause of the workmen. It is submitted that the Union raised an 
Industrial Dispute before the Assistant Labour Commissioner (C) by letter dated 21.11.2017 under Section 2(K) of 
the Industrial Dispute Act,1947 over the issue relating to the unfair labour practices adopted by the respondent 
Management. It is submitted that the union was registered on 07.07.2017 vide Regn. No.508/TVR under the Trade 
Unions Act, 1947 and thereafter in the General Body Meeting the office bearers were elected. It is submitted that the 
fact relating to the registration of the union and the list of elected office bearers was communicated to the respondent 
Management by letter No.ICGEU/BMU/01/2017, dated 15.07.2017. 


2. It is submitted that the 1 respondent has framed the “Transfer Policy-Civilian” by letter no.CP/0518 dated 
22.11.2006 and circulated to the Regional Commanders for compliance. Para 4(c) deals with Group ‘B’ ‘C’ ‘D’ 
Non-Gazetted personal, wherein it is clearly stated that postings and transfer of these employees are to be kept at 
absolute minimum level keeping in view the administrative requirement and need for manning the posts at various 
stations. It has also been clearly mentioned that in case of transfers being inescapable, volunteers for the postings or 
transfer will be called. As far as possible only volunteers will be transferred to these vacancies. It has also been 
clearly stated that as far as possible the group ‘C’ and ‘D’ employee should not be transferred over long distance 
and efforts should be made to accommodate them near their choice station to the extent possible. 


3. As per the above, Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was elected as Treasurer of the union. Since the Respondent / 
Management was against the formation of the union, the employee Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was relieved and directed 
to report for duty at ICGS, Mandapam by letter No.CP/277/17, dated 31.10.2017 


4. The transfer order dated 20.10.2017 was not served on the workman till date. While the petitioner union requested 
that Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj be declared a protected workman, but the Management swiftly reacted by transferring 
Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj and victimized him by adopting unfair labour practice. Hence requested the following relief. 


i) To declare that the transfer order bearing no.1340 dated 20.10.2017 issued by the 37 Respondent

ii) And to pass such other award/order as this Hon’ble Central Government Industrial Tribunal-cum-Labour

5. The respondent in its reply stated that the Indian Coast Guard Civilian Employees Union has not been recognized 
by the Ministry of Defence, as per CGHA letter WE/0302/Welfare dated 09.10.2019.The transfer order of the three 
(3) civilian personal was promulgated vide CGRHQ(E) letter 1340 dated 20.10.17. Accordingly, the individual was 
relieved from Basic Maintenance Unit, Chennai to report at Indian Coast Guard Station, Madapam as per the 
transfer policy and pleaded that the petition be dismissed as devoid of merit. 


6. The Respondent filed the following documents in support of their contention 


Exhibit No. Date Description 

Ex.M1 18.04.2018 Nature of duties carried out by Indian Coast Guard Base 
Maintenance Unit (Chennai) 

Ex.M2 09.10.2019 Service Association and Welfare in Indian Coast Guard 

Ex.M3 22.11.2006 Transfer Policy - Civilians 


7. Heard both learned counsel and perused the records. The point arised for determination is whether the transfer of 
Shri P. Ayan Aurl Raj, Radio/Radar Fitter as ICGS, Mandapam is an not existing post at ICGS, Mandapam is legal 
and justify? If not, what relief is Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj, Radio/Radar fitter is entitled to? 


8. The claimant in its claim statement stated that the following points regarding the transfer policy. 


(a) Posting and transfer are to be kept at the absolute minimum level 
(b) Volunteers for the postings of the transfer called and will be transferred 
(c) Group ‘C’ and ‘D’ employees should not be transferred over long distance 


9. In petition claim the hardships caused to transferring described as under 


(a) Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was transferred during October,2017 quite impossible for getting admission for his 
school going children at the new station 

(b) The workman unable to shift his family in the midst of the academic year 

(c) The employee kept the family in Chennai for his child to complete the studies in the academic year but the 
Estate Office, CPWD directed him to vacate the quarters and threatened to impose a penalty 

(d) The employee Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj fell sick because of the mental agony and remains on leave on medical 
ground from 1.11.2017 to 28.6.2018 

(e) When the workman reported for duty on 29.06.2018 at the Mandapam station, the 31 Respondent directed 


him to report for duty in Chennai for four days in a week. 


10. On perusal of whole the claim statement, the claimant nowhere stated that Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj was transferred 
to a non-existing post at ICGS Mandapam. On perusal of the claim statement, it appears that the Respondent did not 
violate the transfer policy, as the Mandapam station is not far away from Chennai station. 


11. It is the fundamental duty of transferring employee to seek the permission to overstay at Govt. accommodation by 
mentioning the sufficient reasons for occupation of the allotted house. In claim petition this facts nowhere mention 
that any application mentioning sufficient reasons for over staying at the allotted house was made or not. In this 
situation it can be presumed that no application was made by the transferring employee to the authority. 
Transferring employee Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj fails to submit the medical certificates which might have established 
the genuine grounds of his absence due to medical reasons. 


12. It is stated in the claim petition that the employee was transferred due to his involvement in the union, but the 
claimant fails to submit any evidence that may establish this fact that respondent had showed its jealous against the 
employee. The only vague reason given is that he was an elected as an office bearer in the union, the transfer of an 
employee do not appear as a result of his election to the union.

order was provided to the transferee employee. The relieving order issued to Shri P. Ayan Arul Raj dated

v. Labour Court (1) and others 1981 (29) FLR 194 as under: 


“It is well settled that if a party challenges the legality of an order, the burden lies upon him to prove 
illegality of the order and if no evidence is produced the party invoking jurisdiction of the Court must fail. 
Whenever a workman raises a dispute challenging the validity of the termination of service if is imperative 
for him to file written statement before the Industrial Court setting out grounds on which the order is 
challenged and he must also produce evidence to prove his case. If the workman fails to appear or to file 
written statement or produce evidence, the dispute referred by the State Government cannot be answered in 
favour of the workman and he would not be entitled to any relief.” 


In the case of M/s Uptron Powertronics Employees’ Union, Ghaziabad through its Secretary v. Presiding Officer, 
Labour Court (I), Ghaziabad and others 2008 (118) FLR 1164 Hon’ble Allahabad High Court has held as under: 


“The law has been settled by the Apex Court in case of Shanker Chakravarti v. Britannia Biscuit Co. Ltd., 
V.K. Raj Industries v. Labour Court and Ors., Airtech Private Limited v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1984 (49) 
FLR 38 and Meritech India Ltd. v. State of U.P. and Ors. 1996 FLR that in the absence of any evidence led 
by or on behalf of the workman the reference is bound to be answered by the court against the workman. In 
such a situation it is not necessary for the employers to lead any evidence at all. The obligation to lead 
evidence to establish an allegation made by a party is on the party making the allegation. The test would be, 
who would fail if no evidence is led.”’ 


And by the Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in the case of District Administrative Committee, U.P. P.A.C.C.S.C. 
Services v. Secretary-cum-G.M. District Co-operative Bank Ltd. 2010 (126) FLR 519; wherein it has been held as 
under: 


“The submission is that even if the petitioner failed to lead the evidence, burden was on the shoulders of the 
respondent to prove the termination order as illegal. He was required to lead evidence first which he failed. 
A perusal of the impugned award also does not show that any evidence either oral or documentary was led 
by the respondent. In the case of no evidence, the reference has to be dismissed.” 


As the claimant/workman did not turn up for cross-examination, so it is a case of no evidence filed on behalf of 
workman in support of case, liable to be dismissed. 


For the foregoing reasons, the case is dismissed and; and the workman is not entitled for any relief.

FACTS OF THE CASE 

On 06.04.2015, claimant filed written statement stating therein the following facts in brief as under:

On behalf of respondent written statement was filed on 06.04.2016, in which the following objections/preliminary

2). The reference order is itself not clear in regard alleged date of termination. 


3). No cause of dispute rather an Industrial Dispute existed on the alleged date of termination, i.e. 30.4.2006, between 
the Opposite Parties and Ravindra Prasad Gupta. 


Further it has been pleaded by the respondent in their written statement as under:- 


a). The present case has been filed after an inordinate delay of more than 7 years before the Learned Regional Labour 
Commissioner, Lucknow and reference is made by the Central Government dated 17.02.2015 i.e. after a lapse of 9 
years from the alleged date of termination. 


b). The Learned Regional Labour Commissioner, Lucknow, without proper application of mind, contrary to the 
settled principles of law acting like a postman send the report to the Central Government for referring the matter for 
adjudication. 


c). As per the provisions of section 2 A sub section (3), of the Industrial Disputes’ Act, 1947, any application for 
adjudicating any dispute or difference between a workman and his employer connected with, or arising out of

discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination shall be made to the Labour Court or Tribunal before the expiry of 
three years from the date of such discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination. 


d). A limitation of three years for raising an industrial dispute has been provided in the Industrial Disputes' Act, 1947, 
itself and provisions of any extension of limitation period has not been provided in the Industrial Disputes' Act, 1947, 
by the legislature. 


e). On the basis of the above mentioned averments, it is requested that the present reference dated 17.02.2015, should 
be rejected as bad in the eyes of law and as such not maintainable. 


On behalf of respondent evidence on affidavit of Shri Ashotosh Anand, Chief Manager, HRM of the bank filed, he 
was cross examined on 04.05.2015. 


On behalf of workman on 27.06.2016 rejoinder affidavit has been filed denying the averments as taken by respondent. 


On 05.11.2020, workman/claimant has filed evidence on affidavit (Examination in Chief) and he was cross examined 
on 07.01.2021, by respondent. 


During the pendency of case as per notification dated 26.11.2019, moved by the Ministry Of Finance (Department of 
Financial Services), relevant portion quoted herein below:- 


Baroda Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank, Kashi Gomti Samyut Gramin Bank and Purvanchal Bank (hereinafter 
referred to as "the transferor Regional Rural Banks") sponsored by the Bank of Baroda, Union Bank of India 
and State Bank of India in the State of Uttar Pradesh are hereby amalgamated into a single Regional Rural 
Bank which shall be called as Baroda U.P. Bank (hereinafter referred to as "the transferee Regional Rural 
Bank") with its head office at Gorakhpur under the sponsorship of Bank of Baroda. 


Accordingly as per the said notification respondent 10.1 0 & 1B were imp leaded as party, In view of the law laid 
down by Hon’ble Madras High Court in case of Palanisamy R vs. Presiding Officer, Labour Court, 2001 
LawSuit(Mad) 152, and also in the case of Shri Kanchi Kamakoti Peetam Charitable Trust Hospital vs. Industrial 
Tribunal & Others, 2004 (100) FLR 1166. 


I have heard Shri Parvez Alam legal representative of claimant, and Shri Adarsh Jagdhari learned counsel for 
respondent. 


After hearing the parties/their legal representative and Advocate, the first point to be considered the point to be 
consider in the present case:- 


A). whether the reference dated 17.02.2015, is vague and on the basis of the same no cause of action arises on the 
part of workman/claimant to file present claim petition. 


In order to decide the said dispute it would be appropriate to go through Section 10 of the Industrial Dispute Act. 
10. Section 10 of Industrial Disputes Act reads thus: 


"10. Reference of disputes to Boards, Courts or Tribunals. (1) [Where the appropriate Government is of 
opinion that any industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, it may at any time), by order in writing,- 


(a) refer the dispute to a Board for promoting a settlement thereof; or 
(b) refer any matter appearing to be connected with or relevant to the dispute to a Court for inquiry; or 


[(c) refer the dispute or any matter appearing to be connected with, or relevant to, the dispute, if it relates to 
any matter specified in the Second Schedule, to a Labour Court for adjudication; or 


(d) refer the dispute or any matter appearing to be connected with, or relevant to, the dispute, whether it 
relates to any matter specified in the Second Schedule or the Third Schedule, to a Tribunal for adjudication: 


Provided that where the dispute relates to any matter specified in the Third Schedule and is not likely to 
affect more than one hundred workmen, the appropriate Government may, if it so thinks fit, make the 
reference to a Labour Court under clause (c):]" 


11. Plain reading of aforesaid provision would show that when industrial dispute exists or is apprehended, appropriate 
Government can refer dispute to Court for enquiry or if relates to any matter specified in Second Schedule to Labour 
Court for adjudication or make Reference to Tribunal, if dispute relates to matters specified in Second Schedule or 
Third Schedule. It is, therefore, obvious that Reference can be made only when industrial disputes exists or is 
apprehended by Competent Authority. 


13. The aforesaid legal position would make explicit that existence of industrial dispute is a paramount and important 
consideration while dealing with Reference. 


Only existent or apprehended industrial disputes can be referred for consideration of Court or Tribunal. However, at 
the time of taking decision whether Reference to be made or not, appropriate Government need not venture into 


4068 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 9, 2026/VAISAKHA 19, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


merits of dispute, as making Reference is only administrative function. Only because Reference is made under 
Section 10(1), Court or Tribunal is not precluded from entering into aspects of delay and laches or to record findings 
as to existence or non-existence of dispute. 


In case of Prabhakar v. Joint Director, Sericulture Department and "another, 2015 (147) FLR 341 (SC), the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court considered and held the impact of delay and laches in Reference made under Section 10(1) of 
Industrial Disputes Act and observed in paragraph No. 14 as under: 


"40. An industrial dispute has to be referred by the appropriate Government for adjudication and the 
workman cannot approach the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal directly, except in those cases which are 
covered by Section 2-A of the Act. Reference is made under Section 10 of the Act in those cases where the 
appropriate Government forms an opinion that ‘any industrial dispute exists or is apprehended’. The words 
‘industrial dispute exists' are of paramount importance unless there is an existence of an industrial dispute 
(or the dispute is apprehended or it is apprehended such a dispute may arise in near future), no reference is 
to be made. Thus, existence or apprehension of an industrial dispute is a sine qua non for making the 
reference. No doubt, at the time of taking a decision whether a reference is to be made or not, the 
appropriate Government is not to go into the merits of the dispute. Making of reference is only an 
administrative function. At the same time, on the basis of material on record, satisfaction of the existence of 
the industrial dispute or the apprehension of an industrial dispute is necessary. Such existence/apprehension 
of industrial dispute, thus, becomes a condition precedent, though it will be only subjective satisfaction 
based on material on record. Since, we are not concerned with the satisfaction dealing with cases where 
there is apprehended industrial dispute, discussion that follows would confine to existence of an industrial 
dispute. Dispute or difference arises when one party make a demand and other party rejects the same. It is 
held by this Court in number of cases that before raising the industrial dispute making of demand is a 
necessary pre-condition. In such a scenario, if the services of a workman are terminated and he does not 
make the demand and/or raise the issue alleging wrongful termination immediately thereafter or within 
reasonable time and raises the same after considerable lapse of period, whether it can be said that industrial 
dispute still exist. Since there is no period of limitation, it gives right to the workman to raise the dispute 
even belatedly. However, if the dispute is raised after a long period, it has to be seen as to whether such a 
dispute still exists? Thus, notwithstanding the fact that law of limitation does not apply, it is to be shown by 
the workman that there is a dispute in praesenti. For this purpose, he has to demonstrate that even if 
considerable period has lapsed and there are laches and delays, such delay has not resulted into making the 
industrial dispute seized to exist. Therefore, if the workman is able to give satisfactory explanation for these 
laches and delays and demonstrate that the circumstances discloses that issue is still alive, delay would not 
come in his way because of the reason that law of limitation has no application. On the other hand, if 
because of such delay dispute no longer remains alive and is to be treated as "dead", then it would be non- 
existent dispute which cannot be referred." 


Thus it can be held on the point in issue that for raising industrial dispute demand is precondition. In case, employee 
fails to make demand, dispute cannot be referred. 


From the perusal of claim statement filed by claimant on 06.05.2005, undisputed facts which emerged out that he was 
initially appointed as casual labour on the post of jamadaar cum chaprasi in the purvanchal gramin bank, Gorakhpur, 
now known as Baroda UP bank, in the branch saleempur dewaria, in the said capacity he worked and discharged his 
duties up till 29.04.2006, his services were retrenched/terminated, so workman raise a Industrial Dispute and by 
reference dated 17.02.2015, the same was referred to this Tribunal for adjudication quoted here an above. 


Further in the written statement filed by respondent, a preliminary objections/plea was taken that the reference in 
question is vague as alias date of termination as mentioned in the reference dated 30.04.2006, is incorrect and as 
matter of fact on record, thereafter workman work with the respondent/bank.

27.01.2021 he was cross examined, in which he has stated as under:-

था| 


2013 के लिए काम का पैसा मित्र गया। इस पैसे का कोर्ड विवाद नहीं है। 2006 तक जो काम किया था उसका भी पैसा 
मिना था।/2013 के बाव से अब तक बैंक में काम नहीं किया हैं। 2006 में निकानने के बाव 2013 में बैंक ने GE बुलाया 
HR एक बार2013 में मिलाने के बाव बैंक ने नहीं बुनाया। इसलिए नहीं गया। 2013 में Ast बुलाया गया His चिट॒ठी 
नहीं जारी हुई थी. जबानी कहा गया। 


Accordingly from the cross examination of the workman, it is clearly established that he has worked as a casual 
employer in the bank in the year 2013, as such in view of the provision of Section 10(1) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(1)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 9, 2026/वैशाख 19, 1948 4069 


as quoted here an above as well the facts which is stated u/s of the Section 10(1) of the Act, no dispute was in 
existence which is paramount condition for making a reference in question not as per law. 


Further in the present case from the language of reference it is clearly established that the appropriate government has 
referred to decide the dispute that is the action on the part of respondent thereby retrenching the services of 
Shri Ravindra Prasad Gupta/claimant, on 30.06.2006, is as per law and valid, if not then what relief he is granted. 


As stated above in the present case the workman/Shri Ravindra Prasad Gupta, has himself admitted the facts that after 
retrenchment of his services on 30.06.2006, he did not worked for the period 2006 to 2012, thereafter he had worked 
in the bank in 2013 and for the said period he has been worked been paid salary and after 2013 he was not allowed to 
work by respondent/bank, so action on the part of respondent thereby retrenching his services is in contravention 
Section 25F of the Act, is vague in nature as per settle position of law, further in order to established by a workman 
that his services were retrenched not in accordance with provisions of Section 25F of the Act, workman has to prove 
that he has worked continuously 240 days in last 12 months in preceding calendar year, from the date of his 
retrenchment.(See in the case of Lenin Kumar Ray vs. M/s Express Publications (Madurai) Ltd, SLP (C) No.5660 
of 2023, decided on 21.10.2024).

has worked 240 days continuously in last 12 months in preceding calendar year, from prior to date of retrenchment of
